what: The wall-clock limits of this task's evaluation operations (README, Resource limits). Evaluation and the supplied scripts apply these values; an operation that exceeds its limit fails.
hardware: the task's four NVIDIA B200 GPUs at the release recipe (tests/test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_b200.py)

startup.clock: process spawn through the first ready health response, including model load and startup compilation

http_request.applies: one HTTP request, or one explicitly submitted concurrent batch, with every input below long_input_tokens
http_request.clock: client dispatch through the complete response(s), including queueing and first-use compilation

http_request_long.applies: the same, with any input of at least long_input_tokens
http_request_long.clock: client dispatch through the complete response(s), including queueing and first-use compilation

invocation.applies: one measurement or instrumented runtime invocation, including one complete component family measurement (kernels/README.md)
invocation.clock: dispatch through all ranks' records, including setup, warmup, compilation, the prescribed repetitions, synchronization and readback

unit_test_file.clock: collection and all selected cases of that file, including compilation

kernel_build.applies: one offline build of the engine tree: the editable SGLang install and the vendored FlashMLA (kernels/build.py), for the candidate and the reference alike

component_check.applies: one component correctness check of the kernel interfaces (kernels/README.md), all of its cases
component_check.clock: process start through the last case's outputs, including setup, compilation and readback; the evaluation's own comparison of those outputs runs after it, outside the limit

action.applies: a non-inference action, for example a cache flush or a server-information read

teardown.applies: stopping a server or worker group
teardown.clock: TERM, then KILL after 10 s if needed, including reaping
